title: Impact of vegetation cover loss on surface temperature and carbon emission in a fastest-growing city, Cumilla, Bangladesh
study_area: Cumilla City Corporation (residential, commercial, industrial and educational zones)
key_result: From 1994 to 2019 urban area grew from 13.11 to 26.31 km2, very good vegetation fell from 43.35% to 14.53% of the city, and maximum LST rose from 27.61 to 39.28 C, with an 11.2 C (1.86 C/year) LST rise reported since 1994.

method_details.accuracy_points: 300 per year, 1800 total (Google Earth for 1994 to 2014, GPS field visit May to June 2019)
method_details.radiance: L = Lmin + (Lmax - Lmin) * DN / 255; Landsat 5: Lmin 1.238, Lmax 15.30; Landsat 8 band 10 and 11: Lmin 0.10033, Lmax 22.00180
method_details.lst: LST = TB / (1 + (lambda * TB / rho) * ln(e)); lambda = 11.5 um; rho = h*c/sigma printed as 1.438 x 10^2 mK (standard value 1.438 x 10^-2 mK)
method_details.pv: PV = (NDVI - NDVImin) / (NDVImax - NDVImin), linear, image-specific min and max
method_details.carbon_method: Biomass Carbon Stock Assessment: AGB (kg) = 0.0673 * (rho * DBH^2 * H)^0.976, rho = wood specific gravity (standard) = 1.54 g/cm3; Carbon (kg) = 0.5 * biomass. DBH and tree height data from Cumilla City Corporation.
method_details.carbon_pools_per_class: not reported; no per-class above-ground, below-ground, soil or dead organic pool values in this paper
method_details.emission_calculation: Carbon stock maps (Fig. 2) overlaid on LULC and LST maps; emission trend related to LST by a sensitivity analysis (Fig. 8). No explicit emission formula beyond the stock estimate.
